> The point is that we should expose only information to which the developer can easily affect. So only same-origin data. Everything else is not exposed, not cross-origin nor the reasons why browser just decides to not let page to enter bfcache (for example if the system is about to run out of memory)

Developers can usefully react to cross-origin reasons. In my daily use of the web, it's extremely rare to see a subframe that's navigating freely around the web. The content in subframes is almost always closely controlled by someone. As a dev, if I see, that subframe-foo is blocking, I know who to complain to.

Our goal here was to give a statistically useful signal about cross-site blockers. Right now a site that wanted to learn about a cross-site subframe's BFCacheability could detach all-but-one subframe in pagehide and navigate in and out of BFCache to see if they block (assuming they have no other blocking reasons, which is easy to do). This randomised signal gives no more information than that (arguably less since you do not have any way to choose which one).

I agree it's not super useful to be told that you were kicked out for OOM or because of some other non-actionable reason, although I think having *some* generic reason show up to cover these "nothing you can do" cases is still a good idea. Having the reasons be `[]` when blocking is confusing and could lead to bugs going unreported.

- https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/issues/153

> Cancel any instances of the [fetch](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fetch) algorithm in the context of _document_, discarding any [tasks](https://whatpr.org/html/9360/webappapis.html#concept-task) [queued](https://whatpr.org/html/9360/webappapis.html#queue-a-task) for them, and discarding any further data received from the network for them.

which uses the undefined concept of "in the context of _document_".

Given this shaky foundation, I'm not sure what the best move is here. I guess @smaug---- would like it if worker fetches were also canceled when shutting down a document, but I'm not sure that's true across all browsers. If it were, I guess we could add another vague clause to the above like "in the context of _document_ (including any initiated by `Worker`s whose owner set contains the single item _document_)". But I would not necessarily bet it is true.
